review: The hymn is the advent acclamation: the refrain אֲדֹנֵינוּ בָא מְהֵרָה opens stanzas 1–4 and is the print's own repetition; 1:3–4 is 2 Pet 3:9 with Heb 10:23, 2:3–4 is Acts 1:7 with Rev 19:11, 3:3–4 is Isa 63:1 with Ps 18:17, 4:1–4 is 1 Cor 15:51–52 (נְשָׁאֵר … נִשְׁתַּנֶּה), 5:3–4 is 1 Thess 4:17 (בָּאֲוִיר) with Titus 2:13, and 6:1–4 is Rev 22:20 with Ps 120:5.

5:3–4 split the Arabic's word across the printed line break (سَنُلَاقِي الـ / ـرَّبَّ); the Hebrew keeps the enjambment by ending line 3 on the object marker אֶת־ and beginning line 4 with אֲדֹנֵינוּ, so the reader hears the break as the print sets it.

4:2 לַחֲטֹף אֶת־נֶאֱמָנָיו — the Arabic لِاخْتِطَافِ الْمُؤْمِنِين is the rapture; the Hebrew uses the qal infinitive of חָטַף with the object, the verb behind 1 Thess 4:17's ἁρπαγησόμεθα, since a paraphrase like 'to take us up' would lose the single-event force of the line.

1:4 יְקַיֵּם אֶת־הַהַבְטָחָה — the Arabic يُنْجِزُ الْوَعْدَ الْأَمِين is 'He fulfils the faithful promise'; the Hebrew keeps קִיֵּם with the cognate noun הַבְטָחָה, because the stanza's comfort is that the promise is kept and not merely that it is true.
